# oven_towel — repaired realism review

Evidence: f0772, f0808, f3397.

Changes:

- Marked deformable orthotropic cotton shell with tentative modulus/damping
- Replaced full block collider with 80 thin convex surface patches
- Reduced excessive pleats
- Round 1: generated an eight-stripe textile from the source crop; superseded by the Round 2 photographic bake
- Reconstructed drape from depth-supported corners; separate affine rest drape per instance
- Round 2: replaced discontinuous shelf fold with continuous 16 mm radius fold and gently pleated tails
- Round 2: rebaked whole photographed front, retaining eight alternating stripes and hem; replaced generated textile in active materials
- Round 2: source-ray front plane clears the grasp bar; corrected textile vertical UV orientation; individual area/density mass estimates

Current geometry: 14944 triangles; 80 convex contact pieces. Physical size (local bounds): [0.27991, 0.055444, 0.399175] m.

Physics: Rest midsurface area 0.1501 m2 x assumed cotton areal density 0.65 kg/m2, plus 6% hems. Not a weighed product. Individual affine drapes imply different effective visible areas.

This is deformable cotton, with an unvalidated orthotropic shell description and single-layer rest topology in cloth_topology.json. cloth_deformable.blend contains the single-layer solver setup; model.blend includes an optional disabled modifier on the rigid fallback. The set-level MuJoCo XML keeps collision-disabled rigid drapes as an explicit fallback; it does not validate cloth opening/grasping. The same mesh/textile is reused with a distinct affine rest drape for the second towel, not miscounted as a third item.

Remaining limitations:

- Cloth uses source-ray rest surfaces constrained in front of the handle; raw reconstructed depth differs by up to the recorded correction, not a measured drape change
- Deformable shell parameters and grasp/open trajectories are not calibrated; MuJoCo retains an explicitly disabled-contact rigid fallback
- Photographic textile illumination is only approximately removed; hidden rear-tail shape is inferred

Calibrated images are 1280 x 1707 undistorted source frames. Review renders use the same intrinsics and cam_from_world matrices, downsampled to 640 x 854 with the original pixel aspect. WORLD is metric Z-up; glTF exports Y-up. Intrinsics and camera poses were not adjusted to improve scores. The three open views use a shared +0.7 EV exposure correction to approximate the source phone's auto-exposure; this is an estimated review lighting setting. Manual source masks have approximately 2-5 review-pixel edge uncertainty; they are agent annotations, not independent human ground truth. Rack IoU measures the combined outer envelope, not individual wire pixel agreement. LAB histograms use only common projected source/render pixels, with photographed occluders excluded. Lighting and reflections are estimated, not measured BRDFs.

Physics masses, COM, friction, restitution and textile parameters are explicitly estimated; exact product identity and measured weights are unavailable. A/B grades do not certify dynamics or unobserved geometry. No drawer/rack movement or hood filter removal was demonstrated. The oven door alone uses measured sparse hinge angles (confidence 0.45), f3459 was corrected to 0.621537 rad from the photographed handle position, and f3525 reuses the nearby full-open angle. Rest pose remains a best fit to the calibrated reconstruction, whose depth/pose errors do not permit a tape-measure accuracy claim.

The MuJoCo XML is a contact/kinematic check harness with flat-colored proxy visuals. Appearance is reviewed using the textured Blender assets and embedded GLB materials; the XML is not the photorealistic appearance deliverable.

Rebuild this type with its build.py under Blender. Rebuild and review the whole set with build_all.py. Shared implementation is asset_builder.py, persistent physics/instance metadata is qa_metadata.py, source annotations are evidence/qa_mask_annotations.json, and source measurements are evidence/qa_depth_rectangles.json. Texture generation is not rerun during builds; its output and prompt are packaged. The existing reconstruction replay remains at ../../layout/replay/index.html.

## Connection audit revision

The source model and simulation-rest instance metadata are part of the [connection audit](../../../connection_audit/notes.md). This is not a blanket physics or photo-fit pass. Native contact measurements, failed release trials, source-photo coverage and accepted/rejected pose proposals are recorded there.

Contact geometry uses the authored MJCF convex pieces; open vessels retain separate floors and wall pieces in the revised assembly. Triangle meshes describe the visible surfaces. Source mass, explicit inertia and friction values are priors, not physical measurements. Any retained web3 hold is a display/release policy, not evidence that the asset is supported. Capture poses are retained separately from corrected simulation-rest poses.

The towel is a rigid 1.5 mm shell with separate convex strips around the handle. Left and right shapes are distinct fitted variants. A door-relative weld represents fastening; there is no cloth bending or sliding. Nominal mass is 86.7 g and friction is 0.8, both assumed.
